The two are not comparable: the standard definition reads a balance standing as of this data load and applies no period at all, while the card's figure was computed over one — so the gap between them is a difference in what is being measured, not in the population, the period, or how the dollars were valued. cards.actionability_rationale: Discharged-not-final-billed dollars are not lost, only unbilled: the account exists, the charges exist, and finishing the bill recovers them. The small unrecoverable residue is the coding or documentation gap that never closes. Deliberately below DUPLICATE's certainty and above every recovery category — DNFB is the cheapest money in the portfolio, which is exactly why it should outrank larger, harder items.

Any dollar column behind it is a numerator inside the calculation, not the measure itself. Part of this gap is this platform's own doing, not the detector's: the drill was repointed onto a different cut (proc_group → primary_proc_group) because the standard definition cannot be broken out the way the detection system broke it out, so the two figures are measured over related — not identical — populations.

drill_dimension_repoints.rationale: Procedures bind at claim_line, so a claim-grain contract cannot be cut by `proc_group` at all. `primary_proc_group` is the claim's dominant procedure group (largest share of billed charges, ties broken by name), certified at the claim and transaction grains. Read the drill as an attribution of whole claims, not a decomposition of lines: the detector counted lines in this group, and the drill counts claims whose largest procedure group is this one.
